s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic swelling and pain in the mastoid area with a calcified mass
salient_findings: Hyperostotic lesion of the outer table of the right calvarium
Densely calcified mass involving the inferior squamosal portion of the right temporal bone
Mild patchy internal enhancement and thickening of the inner table
key_facts: 28-year-old man with a history of migraine disorder
Several months of pain and swelling in the right mastoid area
Recent subjective enlargement of the mass and increased pain
Noncontrast CT showed a 3.0 × 3.0 × 1.1 cm hyperostotic lesion
MRI revealed a densely calcified mass measuring 3.6 × 1.5 × 3.0 cm
Low signal intensity on T1- and T2-weighted images
Mild patchy internal enhancement
Thickening of the inner table
No soft-tissue component beyond the bone or dural involvement
Laboratory studies were within normal limits

shortlist.label: Osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperostotic lesion with calcification and low signal intensity on MRI

shortlist.label: Osteoblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Densely calcified mass with mild internal enhancement

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Ground-glass appearance not mentioned, but possible given age and location

shortlist.label: Ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar appearance to osteoma, but with more aggressive features possible

shortlist.label: Mastoid osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Specific location and appearance match the case description

raw.rationale: The presence of a densely calcified mass with low signal intensity on T1- and T2-weighted images and mild patchy internal enhancement, along with the hyperostotic lesion on noncontrast CT, is most consistent with an osteoma, which is a benign bone tumor that can cause localized pain and swelling.

rejected.label: Osteoblastoma
rejected.why: Osteoblastoma typically presents with more aggressive features and higher signal intensity on T2-weighted images, which is not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Fibrous dysplasia often involves larger areas of bone and has a more ground-glass appearance on imaging, which is not consistent with the densely calcified mass seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Ossifying fibroma
rejected.why: Ossifying fibroma can have a similar appearance to osteoma, but it tends to have a more aggressive clinical course and is less likely to present as a small, densely calcified mass.

rejected.label: Mastoid osteoma
rejected.why: While the location of the mass is consistent with a mastoid osteoma, the term 'mastoid osteoma' is not a specific diagnosis and 'osteoma' is a more general term that encompasses this entity.
